relations.note: Chicomecoatl is called the elder sister of the collective rain powers.

relations.myth: Chicomecoatl goes to her home in Tlalocan
relations.note: Her hymn places her home in Tlaloc’s rain-and-fertility realm.
They received joint festival offerings, and her impersonator was associated with Cinteotl’s temple.
Some sources treat Xilonen as Chicomecoatl’s name or youthful maize phase; others distinguish them.

relations.myth: Divine sequence of the maize life cycle
relations.note: Modern synthesis links Chicomecoatl with Ilamatecuhtli as mature and aged phases of maize.
Their divine impersonators and priestly embodiments appear in differing accounts of Ochpaniztli.
A disputed modern reading says a child or impersonator associated with Chicomecoatl was offered to him.
relations.source: Later interpretations of colonial festival descriptions

relations.note: Ethnographers compare this living Huasteca maize power with Chicomecoatl without treating them as simply identical.
